body:
Quiet day — no arbitrage. The scanner found zero cross-platform opportunities across the 82 live gold contracts on Kalshi and Polymarket. That's not unusual: most scans come up empty, and today the order books simply don't line up cleanly enough after fees to lock in a riskless profit.

Gold itself is elevated and continuing to firm. As of Sep 9, 2026, the price of gold is 4,393.125 USD, and separately gold rose to 4,400.21 USD/t.oz on September 9, 2026, up 1.02% from the previous day, with the price up 20.87% compared to the same time last year. That backdrop matches what the contracts imply: Kalshi's Dec-31-2026 $4,300 or above settle contract bids near 0.67-0.69, roughly a coin-flip crossover sits around the $4,400-4,500 strikes, and Polymarket's touch $4,300 in September contract bids 0.64-0.66 — all consistent with spot sitting in the low-$4,300s to mid-$4,400s right now. The move is widely attributed to Fed policy: gold has been supported by markets scaling back bets for a Federal Reserve interest rate hike in September 2026, with odds falling to around 35% from 40% after a dovish producer-price reading.

Worth flagging why seemingly overlapping strikes don't produce free money: Kalshi's gold contracts settle on a single spot reading at a fixed future timestamp (e.g., 5:00 PM EDT, Sep 30, 2026), while Polymarket's are touch contracts that pay out if gold hits a level at any point during a window — a materially easier bar to clear. A $4,300 threshold priced similarly on both platforms is not the same bet, and that resolution-rule gap, plus thin 24h volume on many far-dollar strikes, is the mundane explanation for any prices that look mispriced at a glance.
headline: No cross-platform gold arbitrage today as spot firms to $4,400 on Fed rate-cut bets
